title: Chico Mendes
summary: Born in 1944 in the Brazilian village of Porto Rico in Acre, he became a rubber tapper, a union leader in Xapuri and an environmental activist. From the 1970s he organised empates, peaceful demonstrations in which tappers shielded trees with their bodies. He was shot dead at his home on 22 December 1988; a rancher's son was the assailant and both men were later convicted. Tappers' demands led to extractive reserves, the first named for him.

uncertainty.note: Birth and death days are stated by the opened pages.

where.modern_name: Xapuri, Acre, Brazil (pinned to the town where he led the rural workers' union and was killed; municipality centroid)

importance.justification: Rubber-tapper leader whose killing in 1988 drew international attention to Amazon forest defence and extractive reserves.

sources.title: Chico Mendes, leading Brazilian conservationist, is assassinated

reviewer_note: History.com places the shooting in the backyard of his home in Acre; Encyclopedia.com names Xapuri. Encyclopedia.com says he became president of the rural workers union in Xapuri in 1981. Trial details and sentences are not stated on the pages used. Pin is the Xapuri municipality centroid.
